title: Add sketch-based latency fingerprinting and cross-slice guard
author: Diego Ramos
release_notes: Adds a low-memory sketch-based latency fingerprint component and a configurable cross-slice gating rule to reduce noisy false-positive canary rollbacks. Backwards-compatible; configurable via canary policies.
description: Motivation: Canary detectors currently trigger on aggregate percentile shifts which are brittle under localized traffic shape changes (small high-volume routes or short-lived hotspots). This PR introduces a compact sketch-based latency fingerprint (per-route latency hash) that captures the distributional signature of latency across request slices and a cross-slice gate that requires correlated drift across multiple independent slices before triggering an automated rollback. Design: 1) Sketch fingerprint: a streaming quantile sketch per slice that emits a stable 128-bit hash summarizing percentile layout (p50/p90/p95/p99 buckets + weighted entropy). The hash is intentionally small to keep memory pressure low on embedders. 2) Cross-slice gate: policy layer that observes the set of active slice hashes over a sliding window and computes a correlation score; only if N independent slices exceed configured correlation & severity thresholds does the canary evaluator escalate to a hard-fail rollback. 3) Config: new canary policy fields idle_slices_threshold, correlation_window_secs, correlation_threshold, severity_threshold. Implementation summary: - lib/canary/fingerprint/sketch_hash.go: Golang streaming sketch + stable hash function + deterministic serialization. - pkg/alerts/cross_slice_gate.py: policy evaluation used by the canary evaluator (keeps a lightweight LRU of recent hashes). - charts/perf-canary/values.yaml: new defaults for gate config under canary.policies.cross_slice_gate. - tests/integration/test_latency_hash.py & tests/unit/test_cross_slice_gate.py: deterministic tests for hash stability and policy behavior. - docs/perf-canary/operational-notes.md: rollout guidance, tuning knobs, and failure modes. Compatibility and tradeoffs: the fingerprint is designed to be collision-resistant for realistic production traffic signatures but not cryptographically secure. It favors determinism across language runtimes and quantization settings. The cross-slice gate reduces sensitivity to single-slice outliers but can delay detection of real regressions that are localized; defaults bias toward safety but are tunable per team. Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag gated behind perf.canary.latency_hash (off by default). 2) Canary rollout: enable in staging canaries for 48h, run shadow canary decisions for 7d in production (decision path exercised but not enforced), then promote to enforced gate if no regressions detected. 3) Observe correlation metrics and false-positive rate for two weeks before making default-on. Checklist: - [x] Sketch algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] Policy evaluator + integration tests - [x] Helm chart config and feature flag - [x] Docs and ops guidance - [x] Manual canary run in staging completed - [x] CI green after reruns Related work: builds on earlier multivariate and ensemble detectors (see ENG-6123) and aims to address noisy regressions observed in SUP-7812 incident. Links: Linear ENG-2319 (design doc), incident SUP-7812 (postmortem).
commits: 3 commits: 1) add streaming quantile sketch primitive and hash serializer; 2) implement cross-slice gate policy + gRPC hooks; 3) tests, docs, and helm defaults.
diff_summary: Added sketch_hash.go (~220 LOC) implementing a CompactTDigest-like sketch, cross_slice_gate.py (~120 LOC) policy, small changes to evaluator.go to call gate, helm values additions, and tests. No changes to runtime C++ kernels.

Author: Added note in operational-notes.md clarifying determinism guarantees and known caveats with 8-bit quantized models.

ci_log: CI Summary: initial run failed on integration tests (flaky timing assertion). Fixed test timing and reran. Final state: build=pass, unit-tests=pass, integration-tests=pass (2x), lint=pass, e2e=pass (smoke). All checks green at merge.
operational_impact: Medium: new memory usage for sketches (~1-2MB per canary evaluator by default) and small CPU cost for hashing on window flush. Configurable and disabled by default.
post_merge_actions: 1) Enable feature flag in staging for 48h. 2) Run shadow mode in production for 7d. 3) Collect canary correlation metrics and false positive rate. 4) Revisit defaults after 2 weeks.
notes_for_backport: No urgent backport required; if backporting to release branches, ensure the feature flag and new helm values are added to the release manifest.
security_considerations: No sensitive data is stored in sketches; hashes are deterministic summaries and not reversible. Ensure access controls for canary telemetry storage are maintained.
